collection.source_input_basis: the rendered text of the publication as read on patents.google.com on the date recorded in docs/NIKON_FX_INTAKE.md; the hash is over that text
collection.source_locator: US4099850A, Example 1 table: r1..r12, d1..d11, nd1..nd6, gamma-d 1..6, back focal distance 133.975
collection.attribution: Wide angle photographic lens, US4099850A, Nippon Kogaku K.K. (Nikon), inventor Sei Matsui.
collection.contributor: Prepared for the Nikon FX expansion series through JunLin615
collection.redistribution: The prescription is a numerical example printed in a United States patent publication, which is in the public domain. Only the transcribed surface table is published here, as a native Project; the publication itself stays upstream.

design.product_identification: The scaled patent example has the nominal focal length and aperture ratio associated with the Nikkor 28 mm f/3.5. Product identification and FX coverage remain unconfirmed.

aperture_validity.basis: The imported stop plate reaches the clear aperture of the glass beside it, so it blocks light outside its opening.
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: No field-resolved measurement, pupil sample or illumination evidence is recorded for this prescription, so a stop-dependent match is not claimed.

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: DERIVED: the source states its glasses by nd and vd, which define the helium d line and the hydrogen F and C lines; those three vacuum wavelengths are the Project's sampling set
spectrum.wavelength_precision: Vacuum nanometres, full precision, as the engine evaluates them.

continuous_coverage_nm.note: The source states no operating band; only the three sampling wavelengths exist.

image_circle_diameter_mm.definition: Twice the paraxial image height at the outer modeled angle. Geometric coverage remains unconfirmed.

image_format.basis: SOURCE_STATED: Nominal FX format dimensions used for discovery and comparison to the estimate.
image_format.format_basis: Nominal FX format classification used for discovery. Coverage remains unconfirmed.

effective_focal_length_mm.conditions: Primary wavelength 587.5618 nm (vacuum), object at infinity.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Paraxial distance from the final surface vertex to the rear focal point

total_track_mm.definition: First surface vertex to the image plane along the axis

engine_check.method: Thick-lens ABCD at the primary wavelength through the committed Project, composed from the members' poses

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale
comparison.tolerance_basis: the source states its focal length as 100.0 (4 significant digits), so half a unit in its last stated digit is the finest agreement it can support; the same relative allowance is applied to the back focal distance

f_number.definition: Image-space f-number, the aperture ratio the source prints

stop_opening_diameter_mm.definition: Diameter of the declared iris opening in the native Project

field.definition: Object-space field angles at infinity, as the source states them

verification.basis: MATCHED when the chief ray of every declared field reaches the image plane at some sampling wavelength; the difference from the paraxial height is the lens's distortion, not a mismatch
verification.wavelength_aggregation: every sampling wavelength traced separately; each field's measured height is the mean of its chief-ray arrivals
verification.paraxial_reference: image height = EFL * tan(theta) for a rectilinear projection, EFL * theta for an equidistant fish eye

approximations.description: The source normalises its prescription to a focal length of 100.0 mm. Every radius and thickness is multiplied by 0.28 so the paraxial focal length is the product's nominal 28.0 mm. A uniform scale changes no aberration ratio and no f-number.

The source states no clear apertures. the stop is sized for the stated f-number; every surface of one element shares one clear semi-diameter, the smaller of (the unvignetted aperture for the axial marginal ray plus the chief ray of the stated half field) and (the radius at which the steepest surface of that element has a sag of half the adjacent glass thickness), never below 1.02 x the marginal ray height
The Project substitutes the nearest named glass for each source nd/vd pair and uses its catalog dispersion curve. The differences are recorded in materials.model_glasses.
The source describes a diaphragm between surfaces but states no plane for it. The stop is placed at 0.5 of the air gap the source leaves between surface 6 and the next one.

solids_findings.message: element LENS member L4: the OHARA_S-TIH4 between S1 and S2 is 6.4459 mm thick at its edge, 51% of its clear diameter 12.5651 mm, above the review ratio 35%

evidence_notes: The source states f = 100.0 mm and a back focal distance of 133.975 mm; at the product scale the engine gives 28.010579 mm and 37.526429 mm.
The stated half field of 37.1 deg gives a paraxial image diameter estimate of 42.37 mm at 28.011 mm EFL.
